definitions.definition: ell=max(lambda,0), viewed as a natural number (Int.toNat lambda).
n=ell+1. Index sets below are I_n={0,...,ell}, equivalently Fin n. In scalar expressions ell−2i is integer subtraction.
For every natural r, X(r)=X_r=(r!:C)^(-1) x^r. Here 0!=1 and the zeroth operator power is Id_V.
For every natural r, Y(r)=Y_r=(r!:C)^(-1) y^r.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of U(sl2(C)) acting on V
definitions.definition: U_Z is exactly the integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra generated by every divided power x^r/r! and y^r/r! for natural r; its represented generators on V are X_r,Y_r.
V_K=V(K)=M⊗_Z K, with K-scalar action on the second tensor factor. Tensor products are algebraic, generated additively by pure tensors subject to additivity and Z-balancing.
U=K⊗_Z M, with K-scalar action on the first tensor factor.

definitions.type: predicate on a subspace and an endomorphism over a field
definitions.definition: For any field k0, k0-vector space U0, subspace W0 and k0-linear endomorphism f0, Stable(W0,f0) means for every w0∈W0 one has f0(w0)∈W0. Invariance is this predicate.
For i∈Fin(n), e_i=(i!:C)^(-1)y^i v. This formula defines vectors without yet claiming independence.
X_M(r)=X_r^M is the restriction of X_r to M; admissibility supplies its preservation of M.
Y_M(r)=Y_r^M is the restriction of Y_r to M.
x_M=X_M(1), the restriction of x.
y_M=Y_M(1), the restriction of y.
h_M=x_M y_M−y_M x_M. Its identification with the restriction of h is proved internally.
c_j=choose(ell,j), the natural binomial coefficient.
Q_M=Y_M(ell) X_M(ell).
A_ij=X_M(ell−i) Q_M Y_M(ell−j), for indices i,j∈Fin(n); the displayed subtractions are natural and nonnegative.
Dprod=∏_{j∈Fin(n)} c_j.
d_j=∏_{k∈Fin(n), k≠j} c_k; an empty product is 1.

For f∈End_Z(M), define the K-linear operator F(f) by F(f)(a⊗m)=a⊗f(m). The rule is additive and Z-balanced in a,m, so the tensor universal property defines an additive operator, and multiplication on the first factor makes it K-linear. This defines a function, with its ring-homomorphism laws to be proved separately.
S(m⊗a)=a⊗m, extended additively by the tensor universal property: the displayed rule is additive in each input and Z-balanced. K-linearity and bijectivity are proved internally.
S_inv(a⊗m)=m⊗a, defined by the same additive Z-balanced universal property.
red(t) is the image of the integer t in K; for natural t use its integer image first. A bar over an integer or natural denotes red. It preserves finite sums, products and 1.
T_ij=red(c_j)^(-1)·F(A_ij). Field inverse is the usual total inverse (0^(-1)=0); nonvanishing needed for cancellation is proved internally.
ind(f) is the induced lattice operator on V_K, given by ind(f)(m⊗a)=f(m)⊗a. The additive Z-balanced rule defines the operator and is K-linear by the scalar action on the second factor.

L_Z is the free abelian group on the three abstract Chevalley generators, denoted x,y,h in the original problem, with Z-bilinear alternating bracket [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h. In formulas for the action, the parameter endomorphisms x,y,h are the respective images of these generators; the integral Lie algebra is not defined as their possibly nonfaithful image in End_C(V).

L_K=L(K)=L_Z⊗_Z K=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K in the original Chevalley notation, with the bracket extended K-bilinearly from the integral bracket. The action on V_K assigns the formal generators the operators ind(x_M),ind(y_M),ind(h_M) and extends K-linearly. Its bracket-preserving property is proved separately. This definition includes characteristic 2.

inputs.statement: 0≤lambda<p, with lambda and p compared in Z.
hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, and xy−yx=h as complex-linear endomorphisms of V; products mean composition, rightmost first.
M is an arbitrary admissible lattice in V: it has a Z-basis whose images under inclusion form a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. No minimal-lattice condition is imposed.

For every natural r, r!·X_M(r)=x_M^r and r!·Y_M(r)=y_M^r in End_Z(M). The inclusion M→V intertwines x_M,y_M,h_M with x,y,h respectively; in particular h preserves M. For all i,j,k,l∈Fin(n), A_ij A_kl=c_j·A_il if j=k, and 0 otherwise. With Dprod=∏_j c_j and d_j=∏_{k≠j}c_k one has d_j c_j=Dprod and ∑_j d_j·A_jj=Dprod·Id_M.

U has a K-basis of length n=ell+1, dim_K U=n>0, and U≠0. The function F is a unital ring homomorphism End_Z(M)→End_K(U), with F(f)(a⊗m)=a⊗f(m). The map S:V_K→U is K-linear, has inverse S_inv, and hence is a K-linear isomorphism. V_K≠0. For every f∈End_Z(M), S∘ind(f)=F(f)∘S. Consequently S transports invariant subspaces for any such pair of operators bijectively, and transports zero and whole spaces to zero and whole spaces.

For every j∈Fin(n), red(c_j)≠0 and red(Dprod)≠0. For i,j,k,l∈Fin(n), T_ij T_kl=T_il if j=k and 0 otherwise, and ∑_j T_jj=Id_U. For every K-linear subspace W of U, if W is invariant under F(x_M) and F(y_M), then W is invariant under every T_ij. Moreover ell<p, and for every natural r≤ell one has red(r!)≠0, F(X_M(r))=red(r!)^(-1)F(x_M)^r and F(Y_M(r))=red(r!)^(-1)F(y_M)^r.

For every field k0, positive natural n0, k0-vector space U0 of dimension n0, and family T0_ij∈End_{k0}(U0), i,j∈Fin(n0), if for all i,j,k,l∈Fin(n0), T0_ij T0_kl equals T0_il when j=k and 0 otherwise, and ∑_j T0_jj=Id_{U0}, then every k0-linear subspace W0 invariant under all T0_ij satisfies W0={0} or W0=U0.

binders.type: family Fin(n0)×Fin(n0) of k0-linear endomorphisms of U0

inputs.statement: lambda=(ell:Z), ell<p, and dim_C V=n=ell+1. The family (e_i)_{i∈Fin(n)} is a complex basis of V, and y^(ell+1)v=0. One has xe_0=0; xe_i=(ell−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤ell; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<ell; ye_ell=0; he_i=(ell−2i)e_i. For every natural r and i∈Fin(n), X_r e_i=choose(ell−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and 0 otherwise; Y_r e_i=choose(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤ell and 0 otherwise. All higher y-powers on v vanish after ell.

output.statement: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K invariant under the induced x,y,h operators, W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V_K is irreducible as a module for the stipulated Chevalley Lie algebra L_K.

locals.declaration: Let W be any K-linear subspace of the original tensor product V_K.
Define Zsub=S(W), the image of W under the K-linear isomorphism S.

argument.text: H007 and N002 identify x_M,y_M,h_M with the integral restrictions of the stipulated x,y,h. Their integer Chevalley relations follow from H005 by applying the injective inclusion M→V: [h_M,x_M]=2x_M, [h_M,y_M]=−2y_M and [x_M,y_M]=h_M. By N003, scalar extension F preserves these identities, and S intertwines F with each induced operator ind on V_K. Thus the original induced x,y,h actions are exactly ind(x_M),ind(y_M),ind(h_M), with the stipulated Chevalley relations after tensoring over Z. This is valid in characteristic 2 as well: the L_K=L_Z⊗_Z K action is the K-linear extension of the integral action of the three formal Chevalley generators. Invariance under the three generators is equivalent to invariance under every K-linear combination of them. N003 already gives V_K≠0.

Let W be any K-linear subspace of V_K, and assume L1: W is invariant under the induced x,y,h operators. Put Zsub=S(W). By N003 it is a K-linear subspace of U; the intertwining formulas and L1 make it invariant under F(x_M),F(y_M). N004 therefore makes it invariant under all T_ij and supplies the multiplication and diagonal-sum relations. N003 gives dim_K U=n=ell+1>0. Apply N005 at field K, size n, space U, family T and subspace Zsub: Zsub={0} or Zsub=U. Apply S_inv, using the inverse identities in N003, to obtain W={0} or W=V_K. Discharge L1 and quantify W. Together with nonzeroness from N003 this proves P.

For the endpoints, H003 gives ell<p, H001 gives p prime, and H002 gives char K=p. If lambda=0 then ell=0,n=1, X_0=Y_0=Id, c_0=Dprod=d_0=1, and all the same formulas apply. If p=2 then ell∈{0,1}; every factorial inverted in the stability argument has index at most ell<2. The e-basis in N001 lives in V over C; none of the reduced matrix-unit premises used in S002 requires distinct h-eigenvalues in K. No step imposed algebraic closure of K or a minimal-lattice condition. Thus the conclusion covers the complete original parameter range.
